reviews.title: Best Nutrition Tracker I’ve found
reviews.text:
A great app, you’ll have to upgrade to get the full use.  The free version is terrific at tracking calories, fats, carbohydrates, and proteins, and has a terrific scanner on it and a deep inventory of food foods.  Upgrading allows you to go deep into the macros and the nutrients as well as additional features.
I used the free version for a week, loved it and upgraded to the paid version, well worth it!

reviews.title: Best Around
reviews.text:
[Updated] Hi Ryan,

Thanks for replying to my previous review, and clarifying the changes to the app!

I realize the following is a small quibble, but, here goes anyway: The only thing I wish were different at this point is that I could still search on herbs and spices, and get generic results for a broad range of them. Two examples (but there are others): Now, if I search on Thyme, I only get dried (no fresh), only branded, and without a complete nutrition profile. Conversely, when I search on Basil, there is no dried at all, only fresh. The incomplete herb and spice results make it harder to enter recipes.

I think you used to include search results now found in the U.S.D.A.’s FoodData Central’s “SR Legacy Food” category, which has generic entries for both fresh and dried herbs and spices, with full nutrition profiles. I’m guessing there are good reasons you no longer choose to use that database, but it’s a shame it has eliminated many of the previously available herb and spice results, fresh and dried, with their full nutrient profiles.

Thanks also for addressing my questions about why the privacy and tracking data collection has broadened.

reviews.title: Easily the best food tracker AND I HAVE TRIED THEM ALL
reviews.text:
I can’t say enough amazing things about this app. I’ve literally tried them all. MFP, Lose It, Noom, Yazio, MyPlate, on and on and on. This is by far the best tracker. This app feels like a native app. The food database is robust. The barcode scanning is quick and accurate. It records nutrition data ACCURATELY to the Health app (with propose timestamps, Lose It constantly rounds it to 9 AM or 12 PM as if you can only have lunch at noon). It isn’t bloated like MFP. The iCloud syncing is FLAWLESS. It offers a killer app for iPad *AND* Mac. I can scale how many exercise calories I want to consume (only 80%). The level of control I get in such a simple and beautiful app is unparalleled. FoodNoms AI is legitimately USEFUL. 

Thank you for existing FoodNoms. Keep up the GREAT work.

reviews.title: Good but needs improvement
reviews.text: The app is convenient and I using it. It’s my second nutrition app. The interface is much nicer than my old app but the accuracy of foods is not. The other app was about 95% right and this one is say half the items are higher calories than what’s on the package. The AI feature isn’t great but you can trick it into making the food what it should be. The syncing with Apple health is a great feature but mine still will not sync. Once that is solved it will be a 5 star app . I use it every day for over a month.

reviews.title: Subpar and exploitative, no reason to use this app
reviews.text:
Repeatedly changed features to move essential functions behind a paywall, automatically bills you for a full year after your trial period ends, and immediately removes access to premium features when you stop payments despite you still having time left on your subscription. Lacks basic features like barcode scanning, and changed others like calorie ranges to be essentially non-functional. 

Overall, a mediocre app at best with predatory monetization practices. There is literally no reason to use this over the many, many better options available. Look elsewhere.

reviews.title: App went downhill
reviews.text:
This app was a solid 4/4.5 stars. It was the only app I could find that let me specify calorie and macro goals as a range instead of a specific number. Welp, they took that out. Now you’re always either over or under. They still allow you to specify a range, but it doesn’t do anything except display a faint checkmark next to “over” or “under.” Notably, there’s no feedback about how soon you’ll be in or out of the range, which was the whole point.

Separately from that, the AI features are mixed. When it guesses, it’s invariably *way* off. It does a very good job of reading nutrition labels as long as you are very careful to make sure to crop out any reference to what the label is for. Because if it sees the name of the food near the label, it will ignore the label and make random stuff up based on the name of the food. Also, scans cannot be edited, so if it reports 36g of carbs instead of 38g, you’re out of luck. And it names everything scanned from a nutrition label as “Unknown Item” so you can forget building up a list of common foods.

So of the two features that made this app special, they took one out and the other only half-works. I have an annual subscription but I’ve already set it not to renew.
